promises.opening: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. I am Vaidehi Sharma, the moderator for this webinar. Welcome to the Bharti Airtel Limited and Bharti Hexacom Limited Q2 ended September 30, 2026 Earnings Webinar. Present with us today is the senior leadership team of Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom Limited. I must remind you that the overview and discussions today may include certain forward- looking statements that must be viewed in conjunction with the risks that we face. Post the management opening remarks, we will open up for an interactive Q&A session. Interested participants may click on raise hand option on the Zoom application to join the Q&A queue. The participants may click this option during the management opening remarks itself to ensure they find a place in the queue. Upon announcement of name, participants to kindly click on unmute myself in the pop-up screen and start asking the question post-introduction. With this, I would now like to hand over to Mr. Soumen Ray for his opening remarks. Soumen Ray – Group Chief Financial Officer, Bharti Airtel Limited Thank you, Vaidehi. Welcome to the Q2 FY2027 Earnings call. I have with me Gopal, Shashwat, Akhil, and Naval. I will start with an update on our Q2 performance, then move to our portfolio, including new growth bets post which I will hand over to Shashwat to talk about our India business, including the strategic priorities. We delivered another quarter of strong and consistent performance across India and Africa. Consolidated revenue came in at about Rs.60,900 Crores, growing 4% sequentially. Africa delivered yet another solid performance with constant currency revenue growth of 6.7% sequentially. India, excluding passive infra, recorded a strong growth of 3.2%. Consolidated EBITDAaL came in at about Rs 31,500 crores, growing at about 5.5%. EBITDAaL margin stood at 51.7%. Capex for the quarter was about Rs.12,500 Crores, leading to a robust operating free cash flow, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, of over Rs.19,000 Crores. Our strong performance continues to be enabled by sharper execution, operational discipline, and continued cost efficiencies through War on Waste. India EBITDAaL, excluding passive infra, came in at over Rs.20,400 crores, growing 4%. EBITDAaL margin stood at 52.7%, a 0.4% improvement. Capex for the quarter was Rs.7,430 Crores. Operating free cash flow, which is EBITDAaL minus capex, was almost at about Rs.13,000 Crores. In addition, we invested about 2,900 Crores in a strategic land parcel to pursue our one-gigawatt data center capacity ambition. You will hear more on this in the quarters to come. India Mobile delivered another quarter of strong growth, underpinned by continued portfolio premiumization. Homes maintained its growth momentum, aided by our convergence strategy. Airtel business continued to perform well, while our digital portfolio sustained strong double-digit growth. More details on our strategy will be shared by Shashwat. Our consolidated Net debt to EBITDAaL improved to about 0.70, with India excluding passive now below 1, at 0.96. Prudent capital allocation, disciplined capex and continued operational excellence underpins the strength of our balance sheet. Our diversified and resilient portfolio continues to deliver strongly, and I will explain that. Performance across India and Africa was strong. Africa now accounts for about 30.5% of our revenues, India mobile about 51%, India non-mobile is about 13%, and Indus at 6%. We are building a future-ready Airtel by deepening our digital network capabilities strengthening the core portfolio and scaling digital growth engines. Let me move on to the new growth bets and let me start with our financial services portfolio. First, on Airtel Money, as mentioned in the last quarter call, we went live with our lending services in Q2. The business is gaining strong momentum as we expand our offerings to newer geographies.
